description: Everything on the connected user's plate right now — the answer to "what's on my plate?" / "what should I do today?". One merged list, exactly what the app's My-tasks page shows: tickets assigned to them or their teams, orders they should fulfill, stocktaking rooms to count, low-stock restock signals, maintenance-run batches (one row per plan with openCount) and pending setup handovers. section "mine" = act on it; section "team" = a teammate took team work over (holder says who). The maintenance row REPLACES the plan's individual run tickets in section "mine" — they are deliberately absent from this list, because the PLAN is what a person acts on and thirty near-identical check tickets are not: name the plan and its openCount ("Beamer-Wartung, 10 open, earliest due 14 July") and never invent the per-check rows behind it. The one exception is section "team": run tickets a teammate took over stay individual rows there, because the holder is per-ticket. Rows carry the ids for follow-up calls (ticketId, orderId, planId, sessionId, ...) — those are machine handles: name the row by its title and its record link, never by reading an id aloud. Dates come twice, epoch and ISO twin: `dueAtIso` is a plain calendar day, `sinceIso` is the UTC instant the work started waiting (despite the name, `sinceMs` is a moment, not a duration). Read the ISO one; this server does no timezone conversion, so never re-zone a calendar day. An empty list means nothing is on their plate — not an error.
name: my_tasks

tasks.description: Your to-do rows. Each row also carries its own payload ids (ticketId, orderId, itemId, …) for follow-up calls.

dueAtIso.description: The due date as a plain calendar day, "YYYY-MM-DD" — read THIS one, and do not re-zone a day into the previous evening

holder.description: Who took it over, for team rows

section.description: "mine" = act on it; "team" = a teammate took it over

sinceIso.description: The same moment as an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp — read THIS one; the server does no timezone conversion

sinceMs.description: When this started waiting for you, epoch milliseconds. A MOMENT despite the name, not a duration

source.description: What generated the task (ticket, order, restock, setup, …)

title.description: Task title, when it has one

viaTeamName.description: Team that routed it to you

title: My tasks
